koreterm 1.3.150

- Export to Remote Desktop File (.rdp) in a Remote Desktop tab's
  right-click menu and in the Profiles list's menu (Settings): the
  connection as a standard Windows .rdp file that mstsc.exe opens, with
  its server, port, user name and quality settings. The password is not
  written: Remote Desktop asks for it.
- "Keep reconnecting if the connection drops" in a Remote Desktop
  connection's window (off by default): a session that drops tries three
  sign-ins, then waits 5, 15, 30 and then 60 minutes between tries, and
  waits for the network as long as it takes. Once a whole round is refused
  (a changed password, say) it tries once a pause. Reconnect in the tab's
  menu tries at once. It stops for a sign-out, a session another
  connection took, or an account the server refuses.
- A Remote Desktop tab whose first connection fails retries once by itself
  a few seconds later, instead of showing the "session ended" text.
- Session restore brings back Remote Desktop groups, every session in
  them, and sessions that left a group or were detached.

koreterm 1.3.149

- A Remote Desktop tab whose connection drops waits for the network (up
  to 30 minutes, checking the server's port, signing in nowhere) and
  reconnects by itself once the server answers, instead of giving up
  after two tries.
- Reconnect in an ended Remote Desktop tab's right-click menu. Run Command
  and Server Status work in that tab too.
- Opening a profile in a new tab closes the tabs already open from it
  (undo brings them back); a busy terminal, a split tab or a group stays.
- Save Snapshot of Tab and Record Tab in every tab's right-click menu: a
  PNG, or an MP4 video of the tab (terminal or Remote Desktop). A
  recording tab is red, and Stop Recording is in its menu. Settings >
  Terminal sets the folder (Downloads by default) and the recording
  quality: low, normal or high.
- Server Status in a Remote Desktop tab's right-click menu: CPU, memory,
  disks, signed-in sessions (and whether Explorer runs in each), the
  processes using the most memory and CPU, and stopped automatic
  services, with problems listed first. It goes through the server's
  management (WinRM, or WMI over DCOM), so it works when the remote
  screen is black or frozen.
- The Run Command window has Server buttons that work without the remote
  screen: sign a user out (ending the session's programs when it stays),
  restart Explorer in a user's session, and force a restart.
- A Remote Desktop connection can keep an administrator login (Admin user
  and Admin password) for these, and the Run Command window can keep the
  one typed in it.
- More, in the Run Command window: critical events of the last 48
  hours, processes (and ending one), restarting a service, starting
  stopped services, pending restart, a scheduled restart and cancelling
  it, disconnecting a session, and the largest folders.
- Prepare server (More): opens an administrator PowerShell in the
  session that turns remote management on, open only to this PC's
  address, so the Server buttons work on the day the screen does not.
- Trust this server adds a server to this PC's WinRM TrustedHosts (asks
  for administrator permission). WinRM over HTTPS is a checkbox.
- A failed remote command no longer shows PowerShell's CLIXML records,
  and says which of the server's ports answer.

koreterm 1.3.148

- Renaming a profile (Settings, or Edit Profile in a tab's menu) renames
  the tabs opened from it that still show the old name. A tab you renamed
  yourself keeps its name.
- Remote Desktop sessions keep their size while their tab is hidden or
  the window is minimized, instead of shrinking to 200 x 200; a session
  could drop when a profile was saved.
- rdp-events.log in %LOCALAPPDATA%\koreterm records when a Remote
  Desktop session connects, changes size, drops or ends, and why (never
  the server, user or password).

koreterm 1.3.147

- Edit Profile in a tab's right-click menu: a tab opened from a profile
  opens that profile's window directly (a Remote Desktop one its
  connection window), and what you change is saved at once.
- An update.zip left beside koreterm.exe is installed when koreterm
  closes: a message says so, and koreterm does not open again by itself.
- koreterm looks for a newer version on its GitHub releases page once each
  time it starts (unless auto-update = off). A newer one is downloaded,
  checked, and offered like an update.zip you copy in yourself.
- The download now includes an installer (Setup).

koreterm 1.3.146

- Paste works again with a Remote Desktop tab open. Text copied inside a
  remote desktop no longer keeps the clipboard waiting on the server: when
  you leave the session (another tab, or another program), koreterm keeps
  a local copy of it (text, image, HTML, RTF), so Ctrl+V, Ctrl+Shift+V and
  the right-click menu paste it in any tab. Inside the session, copy and
  paste work as before. Files copied in the remote desktop still paste in
  Explorer. A terminal's paste no longer freezes the window.

koreterm 1.3.145

- Remote Desktop groups: Rename Tab on a group's tab names the group, so
  Save Group keeps the name you gave it. A saved group that is renamed
  updates its saved entry. A new group gets a "Group N" no saved group
  has, so saving it no longer replaces a group saved before.
- Remote Desktop groups no longer change the remote desktops' resolution
  (that rearranged the windows open on them): each keeps its normal
  resolution and is shown scaled down in its cell. Under load, a group now
  lowers only the colors.
- WSL profiles: a folder like ~/projects/app is the Linux home's (it was
  read as the Windows home, /mnt/c/Users/...).
- The + button sits right after the last tab, not at the far right.
- An administrator window's tabs no longer start with "Administrator: "
  (the window title still says it), and its menu no longer offers Run as
  administrator: every tab it opens already is.

koreterm 1.3.144

- Remote Desktop groups: right-click a Remote Desktop tab, Add to Group,
  New Group (or a group already open). The group's tab shows its sessions
  together in a square grid that fills it: 2 x 2 to start, 3 x 3 when a
  fifth joins, 4 x 4 at the tenth; free cells say so. Each session is
  under a strip with its name, Interact and Ungroup. The sessions are
  watch only until Interact (Ctrl+Alt+Home or Watch only gives them back);
  Ungroup puts a session back in a tab of its own, still connected, with
  its connection's own settings. Closing the group's tab puts every session
  back in its own tab: none is closed.
- A group is light: no sound, the fastest visual quality, compression on,
  and each remote desktop the size of its cell. Its tab's menu chooses the
  colors (256, 65 thousand or 16 million). koreterm measures its own CPU
  use every few seconds and, with more sessions or more load, shrinks the
  remote desktops and lowers the colors on its own; the header of the grid
  says what it chose.
- Save Group (the group tab's menu) keeps the group; the new-tab menu's
  Remote Desktop opens it again with all its sessions.
- Detach to New Window (a Remote Desktop tab's menu): the session moves,
  still connected, into a koreterm window of its own, with its tab strip,
  to put on another monitor. Its tab's menu then has Dock to Main Window,
  which moves it back, also without reconnecting.
- Hovering over a Remote Desktop tab shows its server and port and the
  user it signs in as; over a group's tab, how many sessions it watches.
- The tab in front has an accent bar along its top.

koreterm 1.3.143

- Remote Desktop tabs: right-click the tab, "Run Command on Remote
  Desktop...". Type a command (or pick Explorer, Processes, Services,
  Events or Restart) and send it to the remote computer's Run box, to a
  PowerShell window on its screen, or to PowerShell on the server through
  WinRM, which shows whether it ran and its output. "Open Task Manager"
  works even when the remote Explorer is gone. A restart or shutdown is
  asked about first.
- An applied update.zip is deleted, also when it was still in use while
  the update ran.
- Favorites: mark a profile with the star (Favorite) in its window, or
  with Favorite in the Profiles list's menu. Once any profile is a
  favorite, the new-tab menu (the arrow beside +) lists only the
  favorites; with none, it lists every profile as before. Run as
  administrator and Remote Desktop still list them all, and a favorite
  connection is listed at the top too.
- Notes for every kind of profile: Remote Desktop connections have Notes
  in their window, and the profiles koreterm finds (PowerShell, Command
  Prompt, WSL, SSH hosts) open a window with Favorite and Notes on Enter.
  A new profile based on one of them takes its notes along.
- Opening koreterm again (a shortcut, the Start menu, the exe) no longer
  opens another window: it brings the open one to the front. The jump
  list, +new-window and a launch that names a profile or folder still
  open a window.
- Remote Desktop tabs fit the window again after a move to a monitor with
  another scale, or a resize: the session takes the tab's new size instead
  of leaving bands of the terminal above and below it.

koreterm 1.3.142

- Settings > Profiles: "Sort A to Z" lists the profiles alphabetically;
  "Picker order" shows them again in the order of the profile menu (the
  arrow beside the tabs), the order Move up and Move down change.
- Settings > Profiles: "Hide built-in profiles" lists only the profiles you
  made; the ones koreterm finds (PowerShell, Command Prompt, WSL, SSH hosts)
  come back with "Show built-in profiles". Their rows now have a tinted
  background, so your own stand apart.
- Each profile has Notes: free text, any number of lines, in the profile
  window (Settings > Profiles > Edit). They are saved with the profile and
  never passed to the shell.

koreterm 1.3.141

- noctty is now koreterm, with a new icon: a core linked to its connections.
  The program is koreterm.exe; your config.ghostty and saved passwords stay
  where they are.
- Remote Desktop tabs no longer drop when left idle: the session now sends a
  keep-alive every minute. After a network drop the tab reconnects by itself
  at most twice, 15 seconds apart, and a login that fails is never retried,
  so a saved password that went stale cannot lock your account. When a
  session really ends, the tab says so.
- Remote Desktop no longer asks about a server whose certificate cannot be
  checked: connecting without asking is now the default. Settings > Shell has
  "Remote Desktop unverified server" to change it, and each RDP connection's
  editor can set its own.
- New in the window menu (the arrow beside the tabs): "Create Desktop and
  Start Menu Shortcuts" puts a koreterm shortcut on the Desktop and in the
  Start menu.
- A profile opened as administrator now starts in its own starting folder,
  not in the folder of the tab it was opened from.
- Tabs show their profile's icon: the program's own icon by default, or one
  you choose in the profile window (Settings > Profiles > Edit): a .ico,
  .exe or .dll file, an emoji, or none. The same window sets a tab color,
  drawn as a stripe along the top of the tab.
- A new tab, from the + button or a profile, now opens after the last tab
  (window-new-tab-position = current brings back the old place).
- A variable set with setx (or in System Properties) now reaches the next
  tab you open, as it does in a new window from the Start menu.
